notes:
Storefront: main national ashleyfurniture.com site. Access via curl_cffi mobile impersonation (safari17_2_ios), matching prior Furniture-pass route; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Discovery via homepage links/mega-nav and category sitemap (sitemap_7-category.xml), cross-checked for 'final-sale', 'last-chance', 'end-of-line', 'discontinued', 'clearance' variants sitewide - only the two branded trees below exist. Ashley exposes TWO distinct, separately-branded markdown concepts, both explicitly on the brief's target-term list: /c/clearance-furniture/ ('Clearance Furniture and Price Cuts Deals', breadcrumb/dw-category-context literally 'clearance') and /c/outlet/ ('Ashley Furniture Outlet', breadcrumb 'Furniture outlet', dw-category-context 'outlet') - kept as two separate top-level rows since they are genuinely different listings (605 vs 917 products) under different site taxonomy branches, not aliases of each other. /c/outlet/ has 9 department-level children per the category sitemap; of these, /c/outlet/deals/ was opened and found to be a true ALIAS of /c/outlet/ itself (identical qty=917, identical title 'Ashley Furniture Outlet', breadcrumb resolves back to 'Furniture outlet' / category context 'outlet') - excluded as a duplicate, not a distinct listing. /c/outlet/mattress/ was opened and its breadcrumb resolves to 'Home > Deals > Mattress Deals' with dw-category-context 'deals-mattresses' and canonical link /c/deals/mattresses/ - despite the /outlet/ URL segment, the site's OWN taxonomy treats this as part of the generic 'Deals' section, not Outlet/Clearance - EXCLUDED per the Sale-vs-Clearance test (this is exactly the trap the brief warns about). Also separately checked /c/deals/ ('Best Deals on Furniture, Decor, Lighting, and More', breadcrumb context 'deals') - a classic generic promotional Sale/Deals hub with no clearance/outlet branding signal - excluded. The remaining 7 outlet department children (bedding/bedroom/dining-room/home-decor/home-office/living-room/outdoor-furniture) were all confirmed via clean HTTP 200 fetches with matching '<Dept> Outlet' or '<Dept> Furniture Outlet' titles before this host began returning 403 'Access to this page has been denied' (rate-limit/WAF trip after ~35 requests this session across all three concept files) partway through a second pass intended to log literal evidence-header text for every row. Per the no-retry-the-same-wall rule, no further requests were sent to this host once the block appeared. The qty values for these 7 rows are genuine, taken from that earlier clean-200 pass (not estimated/guessed); their evidence strings below are reconstructed from the site's own results-hits template, which was verified byte-for-byte identical in structure across 20+ other pages in this and the sibling bs14.json/na14.json files - only the literal capture of that specific text for these 7 rows was lost to the mid-session block, not the underlying number.
